name: Mash-up / Cross-Pollination
deliverable: Unconventional combinations of disparate technologies or business models

steps.text: State the premise: new concepts come from recombining mechanisms that already work in other domains.
List several external products and have the room write the mechanism behind each, never its brand or style.
Pair one extracted mechanism with your own customer problem and force a concept out of the collision.
Draft at least three mash-ups, naming the borrowed mechanism and what it changes in your context.
Present each mash-up as a mechanism transfer, and ask what behavior it changes, not what it looks like.

failure: Half-working looks like concepts that borrow the logo and nothing else: the mash-up stays cosmetic, producing a theme instead of a working mechanism.
intervention: Ask what the borrowed product actually changes in user behavior, then require that behavior mechanism in the concept before it counts.
provenance: Source protocol: the steps follow the written script in the source.

origin.note: Cross-pollination is a common creativity heuristic; no origin given in the source.
